source.title: Rethinking Dense Linear Transformations: Stagewise Pairwise Mixing (SPM) for Near-Linear Training in Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full text present. The supplied text identifies itself as v1 dated 30 Dec 2025; no truncation is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares a different architectural constraint, stagewise pairwise mixing, with dense layers and reports held-out performance. This bears on the broad architectural factor in the claim, but it does not test the specific versions listed.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own Dense-versus-SPM held-out accuracy and validation-loss results. Its theoretical discussion and cited prior work are not treated as experimental results.
record.test_reason: The study compares SPM with dense layers on synthetic classification, AG News, and character-level language modeling. These results test a different architectural claim, not V1–V8. Its width sweeps do not establish interpolation thresholds or training to convergence, and pairwise mixing is not a convolutional-versus-fully-connected image comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: SPM offers computational savings at large width and task-dependent accuracy benefits, presented as proof of concept. Their Shakespeare superiority statement compares different last reported checkpoints; Dense performs better at matched steps 200–800.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces and evaluates a structured stagewise pairwise-mixing operator against dense layers; it does not reproduce the original claim's random-label experiments, width interpolation tests, or convolutional comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and task setting vary across the synthetic compositional teacher, AG News hashed sparse features, and Shakespeare character-level modeling. Width is swept for the synthetic and AG News tasks. The reported Shakespeare training schedules differ in table coverage: Dense through step 800 and SPM through step 1000.

fits_no_version.finding: SPM exceeds Dense test accuracy at all four synthetic widths, by 5.06–24.21 percentage points, with labels generated by an SPM-based teacher.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Teacher-aligned stagewise pairwise mixing can outperform dense layers under a fixed optimization budget on synthetic compositional classification.

fits_no_version.finding: SPM exceeds Dense AG News accuracy by 5.90 and 6.53 percentage points at widths 2048 and 4096.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stagewise pairwise mixing can improve held-out text-classification accuracy over dense layers under the reported recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: SPM has lower validation NLL at step 1, but Dense has lower NLL at every matched checkpoint from 200 through 800. SPM reaches 2.09 at step 1000 without a matched Dense result.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dense and SPM have different validation-loss trajectories; the reported checkpoints do not establish SPM superiority at equal final training steps.

record.problems: The experiments are explicitly proof of concept. No uncertainty estimates are reported, and the listed comparisons do not report training error alongside held-out performance, so they do not quantify the training-to-test gap. The Shakespeare tables have different final reported steps for Dense and SPM.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out from the reported result tables. The Shakespeare BPC columns were omitted because each table reports NLL and BPC as related metrics and the task does not require duplicate metrics that do not disagree or receive a comparison; the tables list Dense at steps 1, 200, 400, 600, 800 and SPM at steps 1, 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error beyond an established zero-training-error width, with training to convergence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local-connectivity contributions, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning breadth, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and competing measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly says paired training and held-out losses are unavailable: Shakespeare Tables 3–4 provide both. Those losses still do not test any listed version. The text states identical 2000-step Shakespeare budgets despite unequal table coverage. Some SPM BPC entries are inconsistent with their NLL values, so NLL is the clearer comparison. No omitted result bears directly on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label comparison using the same architecture and recipe.
Width is swept, but the study does not report zero-training-error interpolation thresholds or test error beyond such thresholds.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison on images or test of local connectivity.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No removal of memorized training examples.
